title: K-Nearest Neighbors
description: Instance-based classifier determining classes based on local majority votes.
name: K-Nearest Neighbors
summary: K-Nearest Neighbors is a non-parametric, lazy learning algorithm. It stores all training instances and classifies new samples based on a distance metric (e.g. Euclidean) and a majority vote of the K closest points.
use_when: Working with low-dimensional data where the decision boundary is highly irregular and training is cheap.
avoid_when: Performing low-latency inferences on large datasets, as prediction scans the entire training set.
pros: Zero training time; model simply stores references to training data.
Extremely simple to understand and explain intuitively.
Natively handles multi-class classification without extensions.
cons: Very high inference cost O(N * D) which grows linearly with dataset size.
Suffers severely from the curse of dimensionality, requiring feature selection.
Highly sensitive to localized noise and feature scales.

key_hyperparams.name: n_neighbors
key_hyperparams.note: Number of neighbors to use. Larger values smooth boundaries but can cross class boundaries.

quick_start:
from sklearn.neighbors import KNeighborsClassifier
import numpy as np

X = np.array([[1, 2], [2, 3], [3, 4], [4, 5]])
y = np.array([0, 0, 1, 1])
neigh = KNeighborsClassifier(n_neighbors=3).fit(X, y)
preds = neigh.predict([[2.5, 3.5]])
